gloss: the five-letter mantra of Siva (சிவாயநம, நமசிவாய and its other orders), the அஞ்செழுத்து
label_source: The verses use பஞ்சாக்கரங்கள் (893) and spell out the letters

gloss: mudra: a seal or gesture of the hands (or of the body) used with mantra in worship and in yoga
label_source: 1093 முத்திரை, 1096 சங்கு முத்திரை; 1094 describes one finger by finger.

gloss: chakra as a drawn diagram (yantra): lines and cells filled with letters and mantras for worship or rites
label_source: Used in the verses and the chapter title as சக்கரம்

gloss: the Lord's holy feet, as refuge, as what the guru places on the disciple's head, and as the attainment itself
label_source: The verses use திருவடி, சேவடி, அடி, தாள் and இணையடி (1551, 1597, 1598, 1604).

gloss: Saivism: the religion of Siva, and in Tirumular its kinds (pure, impure, path, severe pure) and the Saiva who follows it
label_source: 1419 names நால்வகைச் சைவம்; 1420 to 1440 name சுத்த சைவர், கடுஞ்சுத்த சைவர் and சைவர்.

gloss: Siddhanta: the settled conclusion, Saiva Siddhanta as the teaching and the Siddhantin who has reached it
chariyai: the first of the four Saiva paths, outward service of the Lord in temples (cleaning, gathering flowers, singing), the path of the devotee
label_source: The chapter title சரியை; 1443, 1446 (சரிதை), 1447, 1449 and 1465 use it.

gloss: kiriyai: the second of the four Saiva paths, ritual worship of Siva in a form, by Agamic rite
label_source: The chapter title கிரியை (chapter 92); 1446, 1447, 1448, 1455 and 1474 use it.

gloss: sanmarga: the true or good path; in Saiva usage the path of jnana, the highest of the four paths, in which the soul becomes one with Siva
label_source: The chapter title சன்மார்க்கம்; 1477 to 1487 use it throughout, 1478 as நன்மார்க்கம்.

gloss: the graded states of release short of union: salokam (dwelling in the Lord's world), samipam (nearness to him) and sarupam (taking his form)
label_source: The label is the tradition's; the verses name the states சாலோகம், சாமீபம், சாரூபம் (1507, 1509) and chapters 99 to 101 are titled by them.

gloss: sayujya: union with Siva, the highest of the four states of release, in which the soul becomes Siva
label_source: The verses use சாயுச்சியம் (1509, 1512, 1513) and chapter 102 is titled by it.

gloss: silence: the stillness of speech and mind of the sage, as a state rather than a vow
label_source: 1611 மோனம், opening all four lines; மோனர் and மாமோனம் occur in earlier chapters.

gloss: the ascetic's garb or guise: the outward marks of a holy life, true or assumed
label_source: The verses and chapter titles use வேடம் (1655, 1660, 1661, 1668, 1677).

gloss: holy ash, worn as Siva's emblem and armour
label_source: The chapter title is திருநீறு; the verses use பூதி (1662), நீறு (1663) and திருநீறு (1666).

gloss: the disciple, worthy (சற்சீடன்) or unworthy (அசற்சீடன்), whose ripeness decides whether the teaching is given
label_source: The verses use சீடன், அசற்சீடன் (1689) and சற்சீடன் (1696, 1697, 1702, 1703).

gloss: the lingam: Siva's emblem, as the installed stone with its pedestal and as the forms it is said to be (letters, bindu and nada, Shakti and Siva, the self, the guru)
label_source: The verses use இலிங்கம் (1753 to 1758, 1776) and chapters 125 to 127 are titled ஆத்மலிங்கம், ஞான லிங்கம், சிவலிங்கம்.

gloss: adhara: one of the six supports or centres in the body named in Tirumular's yoga (the chakras), pictured as lotuses rising from the root to the brow
label_source: The chapter title ஆறு ஆதாரம்; 1705, 1707, 1708 and 1709 use ஆதாரம்.

gloss: the sun: in Tirumular both the sun of the cosmos, worshipper and form of the Lord, and the sun within the yogic body
label_source: The chapter titles ஆதித்த நிலை, அண்டாதித்தன், பிண்டாதித்தன்; 1977, 1979, 1982 name ஆதித்தன்; 1958 names the inner sun பானு.

gloss: avastha: a state of the soul's consciousness, chiefly waking (நனவு, சாக்கிரம்), dream (கனவு), deep sleep (சுழுத்தி), turiya (துரியம்) and the beyond (அதீதம்), each in Tirumular divided into the others and matched to tattvas, malas and places in the body
label_source: The verses of this chapter name the states (நனவு, கனவு, சுழுத்தி, துரியம், அதீதம்); அவத்தை is the term the neighbouring verses use (2160, 2166) and the title of chapter 161.

gloss: the three gunas, sattva, rajas and tamas, the qualities of prakriti; in Tirumular matched with the states of waking, dream and deep sleep
label_source: Chapter title; verse 2296 names சாத்திகம், இராசதம், தாமதம்

gloss: the cosmic egg; a world-sphere, of which there are numberless ones within the outer egg
label_source: Used in verses 2297 and 2298 and the chapter title

gloss: adhva: the six paths (tattva, mantra, varna, bhuvana, pada, kala) of Saiva Agamic teaching, through which the soul is bound and through which it is purified
label_source: The chapter title அத்துவாக்கள்; 2184 lists the six.

gloss: the six ends: Vedanta, Siddhanta, nadanta, bodhanta, yoganta and kalanta, the end points of six disciplines of knowledge, which Tirumular gathers into one
label_source: The chapter title ஆறு அந்தம்; 2370 names ஆறந்தம் and lists the six; 2371 and 2382 use அந்தம் ஓர் ஆறும், ஆறந்தம்.

gloss: tat tvam asi, 'that thou art': the Upanishadic great saying, its words தற்பதம் (that), தொம்பதம் (thou) and அசி (art) read by Tirumular as the Lord, the bound soul and their union
label_source: 2402 names தொந்தத்தசி; 2387 and 2392 name தொம்பதம், தற்பதம் and அசி.

gloss: the void: the emptiness left when maya, knowledge and their traces are let go, in Tirumular three voids (முப்பாழ்) in which speech ends and the soul comes to rest
label_source: The verses use பாழ் (2455, 2462, 2483, 2495 to 2500, 2505) and the chapter title முப்பாழ்

gloss: upadhi: a limiting adjunct, of effect or of cause, that clings to the soul (and is said to cling even to the Supreme) and must be cut away for release
label_source: The verses use உபாதி (2461, 2463, 2495, 2501, 2502, 2504) and the chapter title காரிய காரண உபாதி

gloss: upasanta: the stilling or quiescence in which the traces of action and the states fall away and the soul rests in Siva
label_source: Chapter title; used in verses 2506 to 2510

gloss: the eight directions, with their guardian gods and elephants, set in Tirumular's yoga as the petals of the inner lotus
label_source: Used in verses 2527 (டிசை) and 2531 (திகை)

gloss: lakshana: implication, the secondary sense by which a word points beyond its literal meaning; in Vedanta, the three modes (leaving, keeping, and both) used to read the great sayings
label_source: The chapter title இலக்கணாத் திரயம்; 2566 names விட்ட இலக்கணை and இலக்கணாதீதம், 2570 விட்டு விடாத இலக்கணை.

gloss: bhakti: devotion to the Lord, and the பத்தர் (devotees) who have it
label_source: Used in verses 2626, 2628 and 2633 as பத்தி, and 2623 and 2626 as பத்தர்; title word of chapter 199

gloss: matha: the guru's seat or monastery, where teaching and worship go on, and in Tirumular its inner counterpart in the body
label_source: Used in verses 2649 (குருமடம்) and 2653 (மாமடம்); title word of chapter 202

gloss: light: the Lord as light (சோதி), the inner light seen within the body and mind in meditation, and the lights of sun, moon and fire he gives
label_source: The chapter title ஒளி (2681 to 2697), whose verses use ஒளி throughout; also சோதி in 2657 and 2670

gloss: space, the fifth element (also வெளி, விசும்பு), and in Tirumular the inner space of awareness and the space in Siva that the knower attains
label_source: The chapter title ஆகாசப் பேறு; 2809 and 2812 name ஆகாசம், 2804 ஆகாயம், 2810 and 2811 வெளி.

gloss: pervasion: the Lord's filling of all things, the elements, the worlds, the gods, the souls and the body, while remaining one and beyond them
label_source: 3026 names வியாபகம்; the chapter title is சர்வ வியாபி (the all-pervader).

gloss: infatuation; the deluded fascination of desire, the poet's word for his own state before the Lord's grace
label_source: text

gloss: devotional service to the Lord and his devotees; becoming his servant (அடிமை, வழியடிமை) by choice, as distinct from bondage
label_source: text

gloss: pride; the ego's self-importance
label_source: The verse uses the word (மால் அகந்தை, Thiruppugazh 76).

gloss: a sacred site or shrine where the Lord dwells and is worshipped; the place itself as an object of devotion
label_source: label is mine: the Thiruppugazh groups its songs by தலம், and these songs name the shrines as பதி and தேவாலயம்

gloss: an oath or vow, especially a lover's or courtesan's sworn promise of lasting union
label_source: text

gloss: the span of life, as reckoned or foretold from bodily signs and counts of the breath
label_source: marker

gloss: reciting the Lord's name, as a practice or as the plea itself
label_source: text

gloss: Valli, the hunter girl of the millet field whom Murugan courted in a hunter's guise and wed, when a song is about that story
label_source: marker

gloss: the gate: in Sivavakkiyar's cipher the womb-door through which one is born, the openings of the body, and the one inner door, hanging or doorless, through which the breath leaves and the Lord and the light are reached
the beginningless: what has no origin, asked by the Siddhars of the letter, the soul, the elements, scripture, the guru and Siva himself, and claimed for the knower
label_source: The verses use the word: 1126 and 1173 (அனாதியோ, five times each), 1128 (அரிந்தவன் அனாதியே), 1145 (அனாதியானது ஒன்றுமே).

gloss: the womb's impurity: the menstrual blood and seed from which the body is formed, named by the Siddhars to shame pride in body, birth and caste
label_source: The verse uses the word: 1159 (தூமையின் முளைத்தெழுந்த சீவன்); also declared in ch063, where 1169 and 1176 use it.

gloss: the breath as the Siddhars' practice (வாசியோகம்): the controlled breath that is ridden like a horse, the word also meaning horse
label_source: the verses use the word (1235, as tradition reads it; in 1204 it means horse)

gloss: the whirl-point: the central channel and its opening at the brow or crown, where the breath of sun and moon becomes one
label_source: the verses use சுழிமுனை and முனைச்சுழி (1299, 1302, 1304); சுழுமுனை is the standard form

gloss: the subtle: the hidden inner thing or secret the Siddhar points to and the reciter misses, named but not explained
label_source: the verses use the word (1293, 1300, 1302, 1307, 1310)

gloss: the maiden: the young goddess as the power in the body, the flame in the wick, in Siddhar cipher the kundalini or the breath at the whirl-point
label_source: the verses use the word (1300, 1304, 1305, 1310, 1312)

gloss: ritual pollution: menstrual pollution, saliva, birth and death pollution, and the rules of purification around them
label_source: Used in 1429 as தீட்டம், தீட்டு; 1423 and 1442 use எச்சில் and 1424 uses தொடக்கு for the same idea

gloss: alchemy (also இரசவாதம், வேதை): the claimed transmutation of base metals to silver and gold, with its drugs, salts and calcined preparations; a Siddhar science, recorded here as history
label_source: 1476 uses வாதம் (வாதம்செய்வேன்) in this sense; the full word இரசவாதம் is the common name

gloss: Brahman: the Supreme (also பரப்பிரமம், பராபரம்) from which gods, lives and eggs issue and into which mind, breath and worlds are absorbed; Kakapusundar's name for the goal of the whole practice
label_source: Used in nearly every verse, as பிரமம் (2329, 2340), பரப்பிரமம் (2334, 2336) and பராபரம் (2326, 2364)

gloss: the crown of the egg: the top of the head taken as the summit of the cosmos, the one place where body and universe are the same egg and where the mind is to be fixed
label_source: Used as அண்ட வுச்சி in 2327, 2329, 2331, 2336, 2337, 2338, 2342, 2344 and throughout the work

gloss: kalpa: the rejuvenating preparation of the medical siddhas, which keeps the body from ageing, and the inner practice that is said to replace it
label_source: Used in 2340, 2341 and 2383

gloss: the Siddhars' cipher: the coded vocabulary (sun and moon, horse, serpent, numbers, salt, elephant) in which their texts name substances, body-places and practices
label_source: Used in 2393, where Kakapusundar blames the other siddhas for writing in it

gloss: the cosmos (அண்டம்) and the body (பிண்டம்) as one: the Siddhars' doctrine that what is in the universe is in the body, so that the body is the field of knowledge and practice
label_source: 2412 says அண்டத்திற் பிண்டமாகும், the cosmos becomes the body; the compound அண்டபிண்டம் is used elsewhere in the corpus (Pattinathar, Pambatti, Valmiki).

gloss: fullness: the whole that the Siddhars call God, defined by Agasthiyar as the sixteen kalas kept whole in the breath, and said to be one with body and life
label_source: The verses use the word in nearly every stanza (2426, 2427, 2428, 2429, 2430, 2432, 2434, 2435, 2437, 2438), and 2426 defines it.

gloss: refuge: the act of placing oneself, faults and body included, under the Lord's protection, said at his feet
label_source: The unit's own word, repeated eighteen times (அடைக்கலம், நின் அடைக்கலம், அடியநின் அடைக்கலம், அடைக்கல முனக்கே) and once as அபயம்

gloss: the void: the Siddhars' name for the emptiness of all that appears, and for the open ground in which it appears, distinguished from பாழ் as the term the verses use for the appearances themselves rather than the residue left after maya is gone
label_source: the verse uses the word (1729 சூனியங் கண்டாயே)

gloss: concord among faiths: the Siddhar stance that the one Lord stands behind the many sects and sees no difference among them, so that the seeker takes no side
label_source: The verses use the word: 2151 சமரசமாயிருந்து, with 2148 பேதமும் காணாப் பெருஞ்சமயம்.

gloss: the appointed meeting place of secret lovers, by day (பகற்குறி) or by night (இரவுக்குறி)
label_source: the colophons' word; the verses name day and night meetings

gloss: the hero-stone set up for a warrior who fell, crowned, inscribed with his name and worshipped
label_source: the verses use the word: நடுகல் in 261 line 15; the stone also in 263 line 8 (கல்லே), 264 line 4 (கல்லும்) and 265 line 5 (கல்ஆ யினையே)

gloss: the gift a bard seeks from a patron, and the asking for it
label_source: the colophons use the word: பரிசில் கடாநிலை for poem 11; பரிசிலர் in 14 line 10

gloss: marriage as the end of secret love; the friend's pressing of the lover to marry (வரைவு கடாயது)
label_source: the colophons' word (வரைவு கடாயது); the verses imply it

gloss: the diviner of Murugu, whom the mother calls when she reads the girl's lovesickness as possession
label_source: the verse's word (Akananuru 232, line 14)

gloss: the velan's rite of possession by Murugu, and the ground where it is performed
label_source: the verse's word (Akananuru 242, line 11: வெறிஅயர் வியன்களம்)

gloss: the guide poem: one who has received a patron's gift directs another seeker to the patron, describing the road and promising the gift
label_source: text: the colophon thurai, and முருகாற்றுப் படுத்த in line 244

gloss: widowhood and its observances: cut hair, no bangles, alli food, the gravel bed
label_source: label is ours; the colophons call the situation தாபதநிலை, and the poems name its signs (அல்லி உணவின், கூந்தல் கொய்து, வளையில் வறுங்கை)

gloss: the state of helpless grief after a patron's or lord's death, and the lament that voices it
label_source: 113 line 5 (கையற்று) and the colophon thurai of 112 to 120

gloss: the battlefield sung as a threshing floor: a bard praises a king's battle as ploughing and harvest and asks for a share
label_source: the colophon thurai மறக்களவழி (368 to 371, 373); 373 adds ஏர்க்கள உருவகம், and 372 has மறக்கள வேள்வி

gloss: the small drum of the porunar bards, and the bard who beats it at the patron's gate
label_source: the verses use the word: கிணைவ 381 line 20, கிணையேம் 384 line 10 and 396 line 14, கிணைமகன் 388 line 3, மாக்கிணை 382, 387, 392, 393, 397, 399, கிணைக் குரல் 400 line 8

gloss: a king's demand for a chief's daughter, refused, and the war it brings on the town
label_source: the colophon thurai மகட்பாற் காஞ்சி of 336 to 340; the verses do not use the word

gloss: an old house of fighting men, whose sons go to war generation after generation
label_source: the verses use the word: மூதி லாளன் in 284 line 4 and மூதி லாளர் in 289 line 5; the colophon thurai of 288 is மூதின் முல்லை

gloss: the seizure and recovery of cattle herds, the deed of vetchi and karanthai
label_source: label is ours; the poems use நிரை (257 line 8, 258 line 7, 259 line 1, 260 line 13)

gloss: sitting facing north to die by fasting, the death a defeated or grieving king chose, which close friends might share
label_source: Akananuru 55 line 12 names it (வான்வடக் கிருந்தென); Purananuru 222 and 223 presuppose it in the friend told to come later and the friends who go to the stone.

gloss: a warrior's or king's vow, made before battle, that names the penalties he accepts if he fails
label_source: the colophons of 71, 72 and 73 (வஞ்சினக் காஞ்சி); the poems themselves do not use the word

gloss: the season the absent man named for his return, which the friend points to as proof that he will come
label_source: the verse's word (Kar Narpathu 4, பருவம்) and the colophon's (பருவங்காட்டி)

gloss: rule-bound conduct; the codified rules of daily, bodily and ritual behaviour
label_source: the verses use the word (Acharakkovai 1)

gloss: a means of valid knowledge (pramana): perception, inference and the others the schools count
label_source: The text's word: அளவை வாதி (3), ஒப்புமை அளவை (41), ஆகம அளவை (43), பிரமாண ஆபாசங்கள் and அளவைகள் (57, 77, 85)

gloss: the atom, the indivisible unit of matter in the Ajivika, Jain and Vaisheshika accounts
a blessing or wish spoken for another's welfare, the frame of a whole decade of the Ainkurunuru
label_source: the verse's word (Ainkurunuru 1, வாழ்க)

gloss: an omen read from the body or from creatures (sneezing, a throbbing eye, a lizard's chirp, an owl's cry) as a sign of the absent lover's thought or return
label_source: the Tholkappiyam's term for omens; the verses show the signs (தும்மல், பல்லி படும்)

gloss: the vow; a religious observance or discipline undertaken
label_source: verse 10 uses the verb நோற்ற

gloss: the wedding; the rite that makes a marriage
label_source: verse 479 uses வதுவை; 485 uses கடிவினை

gloss: music: the lute, melody, mode and the sounds compared to them
label_source: the verse's words (யாழ் 607, மகர வீணை 608); id as used in the Valayapathi marks

gloss: dance-drama as a learned art, with its kinds, rules, gestures and accompanying music, performed before the king
label_source: the verse's own word (677: கூத்தாடுகின்றாள்; 672: நாடகம்); id as declared in the Silappathikaram marks

gloss: the chaste wife whose steadfastness gives her word power over kings, cities and nature
label_source: the verse's own word: பத்தினிப் பாவை (753)

gloss: the festival; a public feast of a god or a town
label_source: the verse's own word: விழவு நீர்விளை யாட்டு (856, line 2)

gloss: water-play in the river or pool, especially the festival bathing of the town and of lovers in the new flood
label_source: the verse's words (Civaka Cintamani 910: தீம்புன லாடிய; 903: நீர்விளை யாட்டினு)

gloss: the sacrifice: the Vedic rite performed by priests for a patron, and by extension a deed spoken of as a sacrifice
label_source: verse 936 uses வேள்வியில் உண்டி; id as used in other books' marks

gloss: the gods as a class of embodied beings in the round of births, ranked and numbered beside humans, animals and hell-beings
label_source: verse 951 uses தேவன், 960 தேவன், 961 தேவர்; id as used in the Neelakesi marks

gloss: drawing a circle in the sand as a love divination: if its ends meet, the lovers will unite
label_source: traditional name; the verse (1037) says ஆழி இழைத்தாள் and prays குன்றாது கூடுக, not the compound itself

gloss: disclosure of a secret love to the family, usually by the friend to the mother or foster mother, so that the lovers may be married; literally, standing by what is right
label_source: id as declared in the Pattupattu marks (the Kurinjippattu colophon); 1052 does not use the word, but narrates the disclosure from nurse to mother to father

gloss: the prison or captivity, the king's confinement of those who offend him
label_source: the verse's own word: சிறைக்குற்றம் நீங்க (1140, line 4)

gloss: the vidya: the spell-lore of the Vidyadharas, recited to summon powers and weapons
label_source: the verses use விஞ்ஞை (1147) and விஞ்சை (1152)

gloss: old age, as the body's decline and the state no remedy reverses
label_source: the verse's own word: முது மூப்பு (2017 line 3, 2020 line 4), மூப்பு (2023 line 1)

gloss: the herders' bull-catch: young men leap at fighting bulls in the pen, and a herd girl is promised to the man who takes a bull
label_source: Used in kalittokai 102 as ஏறு கோள்; 103 and 104 as கொலை ஏறு கொள்பவர், கொல் ஏறு கொண்டான்

gloss: the herders' round dance with linked hands, danced by the girls and the young men after the bull-catch
label_source: Used in kalittokai 102, 103 and 104 as குரவை, and 106 as அயர்வர் தழூஉ

gloss: the woman diviner who sings of the hills to find the cause of a girl's illness, through whose song the friend may disclose the secret love
label_source: the verse's word (Kuruntokai 23, அகவன் மகளே)

gloss: the world-system of Buddhist cosmology: a ring of mountains enclosing Meru, the continents, the heavens and the hells with all their beings
label_source: the unit's own word: சக்கரவாளக் கோட்டம் (24, 31, 202), சக்கரவாளத்து (183)

gloss: a cause or condition that ripens and brings an event about; the Manimekalai's ஏது நிகழ்ச்சி
label_source: the unit's own word (lines 20, 29: ஏது முதிர்ந்தது, ஏதுப் பல உள)

gloss: the offering of blood or food laid before a fierce deity as a due owed to her
label_source: the unit's own word (lines 80, 85: இடும் பலி, எறி பலி); id as declared in silappathikaram ch017

gloss: the Buddha: the awakened teacher of dharma, his coming in a dark age, and the worship of his seat and footprints
label_source: the unit's own word: புத்த ஞாயிறு (86); also போதி உரவோன் (111), தரும தலைவன் (57)

gloss: the vow of not eating: giving up life by fasting
label_source: the unit's own words: உண்ணா நோன்போடு (95)

gloss: a curse, a word spoken in grief or anger that binds its object and comes to fruit, even in a later birth
label_source: the unit's own word (line 47, சாபம்)

gloss: dependence, the chain of conditions that sustains becoming; சார்பின் தோற்றம் is dependent arising, and cutting சார்பு is release
label_source: the unit's own words: சார்பின் தோற்றம் (163), சார்பு அறுத்து (179)

gloss: a false semblance in inference: a thesis, reason or example that looks like part of a sound proof but fails (also போலி)
label_source: The text's word: திட்டாந்த ஆபாசங்கள் (326), திட்டாந்த ஆபாசம் (329, 334 to 335), அனுமான ஆபாசம் (470)

gloss: the five aggregates (form, feeling, perception, formation, consciousness) that are spoken of as a person
label_source: the unit's own word: ஐந்து வகைக் கந்தம் (33), ஐங்கந்தம் (190)

gloss: the shutting of a girl inside the house once her love is suspected
label_source: Natrinai 68 line 2 இற்செறிந்திருத்தல்; the colophons of 63 and 68 say செறிப்பு

gloss: an omen taken from words overheard by chance
label_source: the colophon of Natrinai 65 (விரிச்சி பெற்று); the verse quotes the neighbour woman's words

gloss: the cremation ground, with its pyres, corpses, bones and the demons and goddess held to haunt it
label_source: the verses use the word (neelakesi 32: சுடலை; 27: பிணம்படு பெருங்காடு)

gloss: a state or course of birth: in Jain teaching one of the four (hell, animal, human, god) into which deeds carry a soul
label_source: the verses' own words: பல் கதிகள் (70), நாற்கதி (75)

gloss: a sense faculty; in Jain teaching beings are graded by how many of the five senses they have
label_source: the verse's own word: இருபொறி (78)

gloss: expiation; the act that answers for a wrong done
label_source: the verse uses the word (Neelakesi 148)

gloss: formal debate between schools, opened by a challenge and held before a king's assembly
label_source: the sarukkam's rubric (குண்டலகேசி வாதச் சருக்கம்); the id differs from vaadham, which the list already uses for alchemy

gloss: the tales of the Buddha's former births as a Bodhisattva, told chiefly of his gifts of body, family and life
label_source: the verses use the word (neelakesi 212: சாதகம்; 224: சாதக கற்பங்கள்)

gloss: in Jain teaching an extended existent (astikaya): dharma, the medium of motion; adharma, the medium of rest; space; souls; and matter
label_source: the verse's own word in short form: அத்தி (292, அத்தியைந்து)

gloss: a perfection: one of the virtues a bodhisattva fulfils on the way to buddhahood, counted as six or ten
label_source: the verses' own word: ஈரைம் பாரமீதை (354), பாரமீது (357), பாரமீதை (359)

gloss: a quality of a thing, lasting or passing, and its relation to the substance (பொருள், குணி) that bears it
label_source: the verses' own word: குணங்கள் (379, 381), குணம் (380)

gloss: transformation: a substance passing into new modes, as milk into curd, while something of it persists
label_source: the verse's own word: பரிணாமத்திரிவு (386)

gloss: the continuum: the Buddhist series of moments through which a deed's fruit is said to pass from a perished doer to a later being
label_source: the verses' own word: சந்தானத் தொடர்ச்சி (602), சந்தானம் (603, 604)

gloss: the trace or perfuming (vasana): the Buddhist account of how a perished moment's powers pass into the next, as scent passes from flower to pot
label_source: the verses' own word: வாசனை (617, 619, 621 to 625)

gloss: the moment (ksana): the least span of time, in Buddhist teaching the whole life of each thing that arises and perishes
label_source: the verses' own word: கணந்தோறு (613), அக்கணத்து (614)

gloss: the Ajivika school of Makkali (Gosala), with its atoms of five kinds and its fixed course of things, as rival schools report it
label_source: the verses use the word: ஆசீவகர்கள் (neelakesi 669) and the sarukkam's rubric ஆசீவக வாதச் சருக்கம்

gloss: the fixed: the Ajivika teaching that what comes to be, how, how much and when are all fixed in advance (niyati)
label_source: verse 704 uses நியதத்தன

gloss: primal nature (prakriti) in the Sankhya: the unmanifest root from which intellect, the sense of self, the senses and the elements evolve, as against the soul
label_source: the verse's own word: மூலப் பகுதி and அல்லாப் பகுதி (732); also அப்பியத்தம் (737) and விகிர்தி (745)

gloss: in Jain teaching a standpoint: a partial view from which a thing is judged one, many, lasting or passing, so that opposed statements hold each in its respect
label_source: the verse's own word: நயத்தில் (820); the sermon's நயன் (120)

gloss: materialism (Lokayata): the doctrine that only the elements exist and that awareness arises from their combination and ends with it, as rival schools report it
label_source: the sarukkam's rubric பூத வாதச் சருக்கம் and பூத வாதி (854)

gloss: a cosmic age: one of the long periods of the world's making and unmaking, counted in succession
label_source: the verse's word (Paripadal 2, lines 4 to 18: ஊழி ஊழ்ஊழ் செல்ல ... ஊழி யாவரும் உணரா)

gloss: the great rice offered and shared before battle, binding warriors to the king
label_source: the text names it: பெருஞ்சோ(று) உகுத்தற்கு (30 line 43) and the colophon பெருஞ்சோற்றுநிலை

gloss: tribute paid to a king by those who submit to him
label_source: the text names it: திறைகொண்டு பெயர்தி (71 line 24), இடுக திறையே (80 line 10)

gloss: the war camp of a king in the field, where the army stays through a campaign
label_source: the text names it: பாசறை யோர்க்கே (83 line 9), பார்வல் பாசறை (84 line 5), வெல்கொடி நுடங்கும் பாசறை (88 line 17)

gloss: the battlefield sacrifice: after victory the king cooks a feast on the field with heads for a hearth and blood for water, and serves it to his army
label_source: text: களம் வேட்ட, line 129, and the rite of lines 24-38

gloss: the market of a city, held by day (நாளங்காடி) and by evening (அல்லங்காடி), with its crowds, wares and din
label_source: text: நாளங் காடி, line 430; அல்லங் காடி, line 544

gloss: the royal city as a whole described as the king's wealth: its streets, mansions, trades, shrines and watches
label_source: text: நெடுநகர் line 556, வியனகர் line 758, வளநகர் line 741

gloss: the cold season after the rains, of north wind and drizzle; in the Tholkappiyam the season of kurinji
label_source: text: கூதிர்ப் பானாள் line 12, கூதிர்நின் றன்றாற் line 72, and the colophon thurai கூதிர்ப்பாசறை

gloss: the road through wild country, its dangers and the knowledge of its signs and rules that lets a traveller pass safely
label_source: text: சிறுநெறி line 16, நெறி line 202, செந்நெறி line 258

gloss: the old saying, the proverb used as the proof that closes a counsel
label_source: the payiram names the work's verses so (பண்டைப் பழமொழி நானூறும்)

gloss: the secret or confidence to be kept from others; its guarding and its disclosure
label_source: the verses use the word (Pazhamozhi 178-181) and the heading மறை பிறர் அறியாமை

gloss: young spring, the season of the love god's rule, when lovers are bidden to unite and the parted suffer most
label_source: the unit's own word (இளவேனில் lines 7, 57 and 121; the kaathai is named வேனில் காதை)

gloss: the war goddess of the dry country, worshipped by the hunters with offerings for victory, also called Aiyai and the goddess of the stag
label_source: the unit's own word (கொற்றவை, lines 64 and 87; ஐயை, lines 4, 69 and 91)

gloss: a guardian spirit of a city or of one order of its people, receiving offerings and bound to a rule of when to leave
label_source: the unit's own word (lines 36, 61, 88, 101, 108)

gloss: the old account of the world and its great persons, told by a teacher
label_source: the verses use புராண (387, 404, 405)

gloss: the wheel or discus that marks a lord of the world, the dharma-wheel or the king's weapon
label_source: the verses use ஆழி (385, 395, 398)

gloss: the lowest state of life in Jain teaching, where souls dwell in dense suffering with the fewest senses and from which few rise
label_source: the verses use the word (1957: நிகோதப் பிறவி; 1970: நிகோத கதி)

gloss: the three jewels, the Jain triad whose possession gives release from birth
label_source: verse 51 uses the word (அரதனத் திரயம்)

gloss: the teaching lords who show the way across birth, whose word ends the sorrow of souls
label_source: verse 53 uses the word (தீர்த்தகரர்)

gloss: the offering of a man in sacrifice to a goddess
label_source: verse 58 uses the word (நரபலி)

gloss: the rite of feeding brahmins for the sake of the dead ancestors
label_source: verses 192 and 193 use the word சிராத்தம்

gloss: the Jain ascetic's limited clairvoyance, here knowledge of former births
label_source: verse 284 uses the word அவதி
